text: This chapter started with what looked like two vague complaints, and ended up finding three distinct, confirmed root causes. Billing's invoice lookups traced to a missing index. Scheduling's calendar freezing traced to a batch job's open transaction blocking everyone else. And weeks later, a provider-schedule slowdown traced to parameter sniffing on a cached stored procedure plan.

Three real causes needed three genuinely different fixes — an index, a transaction boundary, and OPTION RECOMPILE — because three genuinely different mechanisms were at fault. No single fix would have caught all three, which is exactly why Lesson 2's five-step plan insisted on gathering evidence before guessing.

The specific queries and fixes matter, but the repeatable part is the method itself: identify active sessions, find the slow queries, read the plan, diagnose with real DMV evidence, then fix and re-test with a new plan as proof — applied three separate times to three separate symptoms.

The health dashboard and the weekly maintenance job didn't stop mattering once the three bugs were fixed. They're the reason a fourth complaint is more likely to show up as a dashboard row than a department's angry email. Maintenance that isn't automated quietly expires.

This Intermediate project stayed inside one database, fixing problems after they'd already happened. The Advanced project goes further — architecture, resilience, and platform-level decisions that reduce how often problems like these occur in the first place, at a scale beyond one Azure SQL Database.
